data.name: Jyotsvika
data.gender_notes: Jyotsvika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jyotsvika is a Sanskrit name derived from the words ‘Jyot’ meaning light and ‘Svika’ meaning prosperity. This name is often given to girls to represent the Goddess of Light and Prosperity. In Hindu mythology, Jyotsvika is believed to bring good fortune, wisdom, and prosperity to those who bear this name. The name Jyotsvika carries the meaning “Goddess of Light and Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jyotsvika usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of light and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A beacon of light and wisdom
data.etymology: Jyotsvika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Light and Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jyotsvika total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Jyotsvika was a queen of the Vakataka dynasty in the 5th century CE. She is best known for her role as a patron of art and architecture during the reign of her husband, Pravarasena II.
historical_references.context: Vakataka Dynasty, Patronage of Art and Architecture

historical_references.reference: Jyotsvika is also mentioned in the Hindu epic, the Mahabharata, as the name of a celestial nymph, or apsara. In this context, she is described as the wife of the god Indra and the mother of the rain god, Varuna.
historical_references.time_period: Unknown (part of the Mahabharata is believed to have been composed between 400 BCE and 400 CE)
